title: Monolith to Microservices Decomposition
question: Should we migrate our scaling e-commerce monolith into a decentralized microservices architecture?
description: Evaluates decomposing a 7-year-old profitable monolithic Rails application into domain microservices as team headcount grows to 60 engineers.
expectedConflict: Melchior favors decoupled domain boundaries and independent deployments; Balthasar fears distributed transaction failure modes and operational sprawl; Casper seeks a modular monolith first.
keyTradeoffs: Independent team velocity vs distributed observability overhead
Network partition latency vs local function call performance
Eventual consistency anomalies vs database transaction guarantees

title: Complete Backend Rewrite in Rust
question: Should our engineering organization rewrite our latency-sensitive Go and Python backend services in Rust?
description: Evaluates rewriting core ad-tech bidding pipeline processing 150k QPS from Go/Python to Rust to reduce p99 garbage collection pauses.
expectedConflict: Melchior champions deterministic memory management and zero-cost abstractions; Balthasar warns of engineering velocity collapse and talent hiring bottlenecks; Casper suggests profiling and optimizing hot Go paths.
keyTradeoffs: Sub-millisecond p99 latency vs developer onboarding ramp
Memory safety without GC vs compiler borrow checker overhead
Ecosystem maturity for niche libraries vs raw throughput

title: Primary Database: PostgreSQL vs MongoDB
question: Should our newly launched multi-tenant B2B platform use PostgreSQL with JSONB or MongoDB as its primary datastore?
description: Evaluates relational schema rigor with JSONB extensibility against document-oriented schema flexibility for an enterprise SaaS product.
expectedConflict: Melchior promotes relational integrity, ACID compliance, and SQL standards; Balthasar highlights risk of polymorphic document drift; Casper balances rapid iteration of document models with operational battle-testing.
keyTradeoffs: Strict relational integrity vs dynamic schema evolution
Advanced indexing and JOIN capabilities vs horizontal sharding ergonomics
Long-term operational predictability vs day-one developer speed

title: Compute Platform: Serverless vs Containerized Kubernetes
question: Should our bursty consumer API run on Serverless Functions (AWS Lambda) or a containerized Kubernetes cluster (EKS)?
description: Evaluates cold-start tolerance, infrastructure maintenance burden, and cost curves between fully managed serverless and container orchestration.
expectedConflict: Melchior calculates per-request cost efficiency at scale; Balthasar warns against vendor lock-in and cold-start tail latency; Casper weighs team DevOps capacity against operational overhead.
keyTradeoffs: Zero idle cost and automatic scaling vs tail-latency cold starts
Fully managed operational offloading vs proprietary cloud vendor primitives
Developer local testability vs production parity

title: API Gateway Strategy: GraphQL Federation vs REST + OpenAPI
question: Should we standardize our unified client gateway on a federated GraphQL schema or RESTful endpoints with OpenAPI contracts?
description: Evaluates client over-fetching prevention and unified graph navigation against HTTP caching simplicity and endpoint authorization boundaries.
expectedConflict: Melchior values client-driven declarative data fetching; Balthasar notes denial-of-service risks through nested recursive queries; Casper questions complexity of GraphQL gateway federation.
keyTradeoffs: Exact data payload fetching vs native HTTP CDN caching
Unified client schema graph vs isolated service endpoint security
Query complexity governance vs API versioning maintenance

title: Data Architecture: Event Sourcing & CQRS for Financial Ledger
question: Should we implement Event Sourcing and CQRS for our new transaction settlement ledger instead of traditional CRUD tables?
description: Evaluates full immutable auditability and temporal queries against projection lag and event schema evolution complexity.
expectedConflict: Melchior insists on immutable mathematical audit trails; Balthasar fears event versioning migrations and projection consistency bugs; Casper recommends event-audited CRUD with append-only logs.
keyTradeoffs: Complete temporal reconstructibility vs asynchronous read-model latency
Write-model throughput vs projection rebuild overhead
Architectural conceptual load on engineering team vs absolute audit compliance

title: Caching Architecture: Redis Cluster vs Local In-Process Cache
question: Should our high-read metadata service use a centralized Redis cluster or distributed in-process memory caches with invalidation broadcasts?
description: Evaluates 100k QPS read latency between zero-hop local in-process RAM (5µs) and centralized networked Redis (1ms).
expectedConflict: Melchior pursues maximum read throughput; Balthasar flags stale data cache-invalidation bugs during race conditions; Casper designs a hybrid L1/L2 multi-tier cache.
keyTradeoffs: Sub-millisecond memory speed vs cache invalidation race conditions
Single source of cache truth vs network serialization roundtrips
Memory footprint per service instance vs dedicated cluster infrastructure cost

title: Disaster Recovery: Active-Active Multi-Region vs Active-Passive
question: Should our global payment processing pipeline deploy an Active-Active multi-region database or Active-Passive with automated failover?
description: Evaluates conflict-free replicated data types and cross-region write consensus against operational complexity and RPO/RTO SLAs.
expectedConflict: Melchior analyzes theoretical zero-RTO continuous uptime; Balthasar stresses split-brain scenarios and cross-region consensus latency; Casper champions active-passive with rigorous failover drills.
keyTradeoffs: Instantaneous cross-region failover vs cross-region write latency penalty
Conflict resolution algorithms (CRDTs/LWW) vs guaranteed transactional serializability
Engineering maintenance overhead vs realistic outage recovery objectives

title: Rendering Tier: Edge Workers vs Centralized Origin Kubernetes
question: Should we move server-side rendering and dynamic personalization to Edge Workers (Cloudflare/Vercel) instead of centralized origin nodes?
description: Evaluates sub-50ms global TTFB against edge runtime resource constraints, cold starts, and database connection pooling limitations.
expectedConflict: Melchior celebrates global physical proximity to users; Balthasar points out database connection thrashing from edge to origin; Casper isolates edge rendering to static fragments with dynamic client hydration.
keyTradeoffs: Low global TTFB latency vs edge execution CPU/memory sandboxes
Decentralized edge compute vs backend database proximity
Specialized runtime vendor lock-in vs standardized Docker runtime

title: Asynchronous Backbone: Apache Kafka vs RabbitMQ / SQS
question: Should our asynchronous ingestion pipeline standardize on Apache Kafka streaming or simpler message queues like RabbitMQ / SQS?
description: Evaluates replayable commit-log partitions against broker-managed dead-letter queues, routing keys, and operational ergonomics.
expectedConflict: Melchior champions consumer-driven replayability and high-throughput partitioning; Balthasar dreads Kafka cluster operational toil and consumer group rebalances; Casper advocates SQS for simple task queues.
keyTradeoffs: Replayable log stream vs ephemeral push-based message acknowledgment
Partition rebalancing and cluster maintenance vs managed cloud queue simplicity
High streaming throughput (GB/s) vs complex consumer error retry ergonomics

title: Internal Communication: gRPC / Protobuf vs JSON / HTTP
question: Should our internal backend service-to-service communication migrate entirely from JSON over HTTP/1.1 to gRPC with HTTP/2 and Protobuf?
description: Evaluates binary serialization speed, streaming, and strict type schemas against debugging friction and browser/tooling interoperability.
expectedConflict: Melchior praises compact wire format and generated client stubs; Balthasar worries about loss of curl/plaintext inspectability and load balancer gRPC stream multiplexing; Casper adopts gRPC for heavy internal trunks only.
keyTradeoffs: Binary serialization throughput and multiplexing vs human-readable inspection
Strict contract compile-time enforcement vs loose dynamic payload flexibility
Specialized tooling/gateway requirements vs universal HTTP ecosystem support

title: SaaS Multi-Tenancy: Database-per-Tenant vs Shared RLS
question: Should our enterprise SaaS platform isolate enterprise customers with a database-per-tenant model or a unified database using Row Level Security (RLS)?
description: Evaluates regulatory data sovereignty and noisy-neighbor blast radius against database migration execution and infrastructure resource efficiency.
expectedConflict: Melchior models cost scaling and resource sharing efficiency of unified RLS; Balthasar mandates absolute physical data isolation to eliminate leak risk; Casper introduces a tiering model with shared pools and VIP silos.
keyTradeoffs: Hardware pooling efficiency vs risk of accidental cross-tenant data leaks
Unified schema migration velocity vs per-tenant backup/restore flexibility
Noisy neighbor resource starvation vs operational cost of hundreds of database instances
